assumption_visibility.rationale: All key technical assumptions are explicitly documented: Chrome browser availability, Node.js environment, JavaScript/TypeScript implementation, Canvas/WebGL sufficiency, acceptable commodity market algorithms, and basic pirate AI. No hidden or unstated assumptions that would impact feasibility.

evidence_grounding.rationale: Evidence references are grounded in initiative objectives, constraints, and metadata (complexity XS, type web-app). The rationale explicitly cites these evidence sources, and the proposed scope aligns with the stated constraints and verification requirements.

problem_clarity.rationale: Problem statement clearly defines an Elite-inspired single-player space trading and combat game with specific functional requirements (parallax starfield, hyperspace jumps, station docking, ship management, commodity trading, laser combat) and明确的技术栈约束 (web browser, Chrome, single-page experience).

risk_visibility.rationale: Risks are well-identified across performance (60fps target), complexity (combat AI within XS scope), integration (offline operation), and acceptance (subjective visual polish). Risk categories are comprehensive and each risk is specific and actionable for mitigation.

scope_boundedness.rationale: Candidate scope provides concrete minimum useful scope with quantifiable deliverables: 8+ star systems, one station per system, commodity trading market, hyperspace travel with fuel consumption and pirate encounters, ship-to-ship combat, ship upgrades, save/load functionality, and /healthz endpoint. The scope is appropriately bounded for XS complexity.

stakeholder_coverage.rationale: Stakeholders are clearly identified with distinct roles and expectations: the Player (immediate gameplay experience), the Factory system (one-command startup, local runnability, offline capability), and Verification providers (specific test requirements and endpoints). Coverage is complete for the production context.

unknowns_manageability.rationale: Unknowns are specific and technical (market mechanics, upgrade balance, visual effect details, persistence mechanism, AI patterns) rather than fundamental feasibility questions. These are standard implementation details that can be resolved through iterative development and do not block progress.

non_blocking_gaps.description: Exact commodity market mechanics (price fluctuation algorithms, scarcity modeling) need implementation detail decisions
Detailed balance of ship upgrade costs vs. profitability requires playtesting and tuning
Specific visual effect implementation details (hyperspace jump, parallax depth) need technical specification
Save/load persistence mechanism (localStorage, file system, etc.) requires architectural decision
Specific pirate AI behavior patterns need definition during development

payload.rationale: All seven readiness dimensions are sufficient. The problem is clearly defined, scope is appropriately bounded for XS complexity, stakeholders are comprehensively covered, assumptions are explicit, unknowns are manageable implementation details, risks are well-identified, and the proposal is grounded in initiative evidence. No blocking gaps exist; five non-blocking gaps represent standard development decisions. The proposal's recommended_outcome of 'go' and the comprehensive rationale supporting feasibility confirm readiness to proceed to settlement.
